I don’t know why I subject myself to these stupid games.

Every shot feels inconsistent even after hours of tweaking. Visual Concepts clearly wanted Rhythm Shooting tighter this year — narrower green windows, contests that actually matter — and on paper that sounds like “real basketball.” In practice it feels like the game is gaslighting you. Same release, same animation, different result. I’m not dropping another $100 to find out whether the build I ended up with is even remotely usable. Reviewers keep putting that number in the $60–80 VC range just to hang online; if you’re grinding it for free, good luck.

Fire & Concrete is the new MyCAREER story and it’s boring. Longer than last year’s (eleven chapters), more cinematic, same empty feeling. Running Mates / Trace Miller is sold as the big innovation — co-op career, custom sidekick, dual meters — and all it does is add another system to babysit while the story still plays like a checklist. Skip to the NBA if you can. I wish I had.

Street Kings is worse for different reasons: so many non-skippable cutscenes that the intro and win animation eat as much time as the game itself. The community’s been begging to skip that emcee for years. 2K keeps him in. Coincidence that it slows your VC per hour? Sure.

On a fresh build you’re slow, your controls feel broken, and every shot is a joke. That’s not a skill issue — it’s the product. At every corner these developers have added grind for the sake of grind. Leveling takes forever no matter what you’re doing. Want MyCAREER Eras too? Congrats: a separate low-60s player for each era, more VC, more time, more reasons to open the store. Progression isn’t a curve. It’s a funnel toward the wallet.

Online is full of Chronus users and cheaters, so there’s literally no point competing “fair.” Even if you ignore that, the City meta still rewards whoever paid first.

The part that actually breaks me: after 40 grueling hours I still haven’t been able to properly work through even the basic systems. They obfuscate what every stat does and what will or won’t affect a shot. You’re supposed to “learn the game,” but the UI won’t teach you — it just wants you to keep playing until you either get it or pay to skip the confusion.

The on-court basketball might be sharper. The career around it is still a cash cow wrapped in cutscenes. Frustrating, opaque, and not worth the time or the money.

A game where feedback is only heard from content creators and twitch streamers, who cried and cried that it's ridiculous that some simple pleb can you know, just, press a button and dunk. "Here I am sir 2k sir, on a stream with 200k followers and this brown shirt just dunked in my face, stop that clowntown". Well 2k has freaking delivered. Forced layup and dunk meter introduced is probably the worst feature ever in sports gaming history, and we had some baddies here including directional stick shooting for a moment. The way it works is that game decides what animation are you going to get at any given time, and that combined with game deciding what animation is defender going to get, will result in variance in whether you should release faster, slower, or how tight the window is. This practically results in just the worst subjective feeling of randomness ever. There's nothing you can do and game, and its developers are just laughing in your face. I mean quite literally, Mike Wang is trolling people on Twitter and telling them to 'git gud'. Some people just want to play simulated basketball and not train Street Fighter level sequences just to not brick layups.

Game does play reasonably OK when shooting meters are disabled, but this is not possible for online game modes, and large number of people just doesn't like to play that way either. Nba Live '97 had shooting figured out 30 years ago, it's unbelievable that this is a problem today.

They have really taken it to the absolute extreme and game is catering exclusively to streamers and content creators.

Frankly, this game is frustrating on so many levels.

First, the shooting feels incredibly inconsistent, especially online. I’m perfectly fine with defense being stronger and more consistent than it was in 2K26 — in fact, I think that’s one of the better changes this year. But making defense better does not justify making shooting feel unreliable.

Even when you create a genuinely good look, get an Open or Wide Open shot and feel like you timed it correctly, the game can still give you an Early or Late release that doesn’t seem to match your input. Making good offense harder is one thing. Making open shots feel inconsistent is another. At times, it genuinely feels like the game punishes good shot selection while rewarding questionable shots.

Second, MyCAREER is once again more of the same, except now you have a Running Mate tied to the storyline. It sounds like a cool addition on paper until you realize that this mechanic is mandatory if you want to progress through the story. At that point, I’d honestly rather play MyNBA with a created player and customize him exactly the way I want.

The animation library is another major disappointment. There are some new and revamped animations, but after playing for this long, it honestly feels like the overwhelming majority of what you see has been recycled from previous games. For a yearly AAA release, that makes the game feel far less fresh than it should.

Long-term progression is also less rewarding than it used to be. Build Specializations are an interesting idea, and the new badge system has some genuinely good concepts, but the amount of grinding required often kills the excitement. There are more options, yet the progression itself feels increasingly designed around keeping you playing rather than simply making the game more enjoyable.

The WNBA side is disappointing as well. I know it has never received the same level of attention as the NBA side, and 2K has made some effort to bring its builder closer to MyCAREER, but I honestly preferred the old system.

And then you have all the usual 2K problems: an uninspired City, a rough Early Access period, a messy launch, bugs, glitches, cheaters, and a general feeling that many longstanding issues are allowed to survive from one game to the next.

The lack of real competition in the basketball gaming market clearly doesn’t help. 2K has very little pressure to fundamentally improve the product every year, and 2K27 feels like another example of that.

The lack of proper PC-console crossplay in 2026 for a AAA sports game is also ridiculous.

I can understand why some people prefer 2K27 to 2K26 because of the stronger defense and harder scoring. I actually agree that the defense is better. But a few gameplay improvements do not erase inconsistent shooting, recycled animations, grind-heavy progression, technical problems and the same issues that have been following this series for years.

I genuinely tried to adapt to the shooting, the progression systems and the new mechanics, but eventually I realized I simply wasn’t having fun anymore, so I uninstalled the game.

I’ve been playing 2K since 2K20. I’m not a newcomer struggling to learn the mechanics — I’ve played enough of this series to know the difference between a demanding shooting system and one that simply feels inconsistent. I've watched so many videos of how to play online from passionate 2K youtubers, trying to improve every year. But since 2K25, it’s started to feel less like I’m improving at a basketball game and more like I’m stuck in an endless yearly loop of relearning systems that keep changing for the sake of changing. I’m finally trying to break out of it.

And then there’s the monetization. I’m done spending hundreds of euros every year between the game itself, builds and cosmetics. Basic clothing items can cost over 10,000 VC each, with some individual pieces going past 20,000 or even 30,000 VC. That is absurd for a full-priced yearly release, especially when you’re already expected to spend heavily on builds if you want to experiment with different playstyles.

At some point, this stops feeling like optional customization and starts feeling like an economy designed to constantly push you toward spending more. I’m simply not willing to throw hundreds of euros at the same yearly cycle anymore.

I genuinely don’t understand the amount of praise this game is getting when so many of its longstanding problems are still here.

First off, I only play MyNBA and thus my review is based on that alone. 

While I recommended the game, it comes with a large caveat that MyNBA continues to be broken if played beyond 4 or 5 seasons and you need to know what is broken, what the work arounds are, and be willing to spend the extra time and control all the teams during specific periods for the work arounds. 
An example of this, teams' staff budgets and staff hiring is significantly broken. Well over half the teams never have enough staff budget to hire and actual coach and so they get stuck hiring a coach with a rating of 25 offense and 25 defense and no other badges or anything helpful. Then all the actual coaches just sit there not being hired. The work around is to control all teams during staff signing period, in the off season, and make the offers for them. This way (it does not work during the season) you can offer the bare minimum and because they don't have any other offers they will accept it. For some reason, the computer won't make these bare minimum offers to actual coaches. There  are more needed work arounds but that is just an example. 
 
Staff:
1) There is ZERO coach tracking. They put a decent amount of resources into the coaches but then do nothing to connect you to them. There is NO stats, win/loss, championships, awards history, coaching trees, etc....absolutely nothing to bring any depth to coaches beyond their buffs. Even Madden gives you a win/loss and championships for their coaches. We need stats and coaching trees, so coaches are part of the story rather than some passive background buff.
2) Staff progression is done automatically behind the scenes and players have ZERO connection to the progression. We don't even know if coaches have progressed unless we remember or write down their stats and budgets. They need to allow us to upgrade coaches within a transparent progression system, much like Madden does. I am super happy they gave us back control of our assistant coach, now let us upgrade them and build upon or start our own coaching trees and legacies. 
3) As mentioned above, the staff budgets are broken. 
4) I'm glad we get to be a GM now and have the governor above us.  

Players:
1) I love the depth to the players and the sandbox freedom.
2) Shooting tendencies continue to reset themselves and not stay where we adjust them for realism.
3) FA is broken. Teams never have enough money to sign FAs. In real life, most stars move through sign and trade deals, as most teams don't have the cap space for outright signing. Sign and trade deals by the computer is non-existent. The result is many players, including stars, get signed for $2 mil on a 1 year contract and will change teams every single year. Also because they get signed for so little, teams can become unrealistic. There is a lot of work that goes into this work around to fix it. 
4) Really LOVE the new historic draft automatic setup. Putting it on shuffle, for random drafts with historical players, is extremely satisfying. 

I will need to play more to update the new morale, relationships, and trust mechanics but will update when I have fully experienced them over a 20 season span. 

My BIGGEST disappointment comes from being super excited about playing the new MyLegacy within MyNBA. Sadly, I found out it is not the sandbox that was promised and you are locked into playing only one team at a time and are not able to use custom rosters. The mode is far too broken (see above for a couple examples) to not be able to control other teams for work arounds. Thus, I will not be able to enjoy this new mode and I'm not sure why they chose to limit our access when they have always been good about giving us full control.

NBA 2K27 was honestly close to being a good game, and that’s what makes this so frustrating.

When me and my friends are playing against legitimate players, the game can actually be fun. I can accept losing to people who are better than us. I can accept somebody having a great game, hitting difficult shots, or simply outplaying us.

What I cannot accept is constantly running into obvious cheaters on PC.

Once again, Easy Anti-Cheat feels like an absolute joke. Players are running around with ridiculous builds, seemingly maxed attributes, insane speed, hitting deep fading threes, dunking everything, defending everything, and doing things that legitimate builds simply cannot do. When you’re playing against that, there is no real competition. You’re expected to play nearly perfect just to stay close to somebody who isn’t playing by the same rules.

That completely ruins the best part of 2K: competing against real people.

2K already has plenty of other problems. They essentially have no real competition in the basketball simulation market. VC is expensive, progression heavily encourages spending money, cosmetics and animations are resold year after year, and nearly every part of MyPLAYER feels designed to extract more money from the player.

I can tolerate some of that when the actual game is fun.

What I cannot tolerate is 2K making this much money from its player base while seemingly doing so little to protect the integrity of the PC version.

PC cheating has been a problem for years. This is now another next-gen PC release with anti-cheat, and obvious cheating is still rampant. At some point, simply saying that the game has Easy Anti-Cheat is not enough. The results are what matter, and right now the results are terrible.

The frustrating part is that there is a genuinely enjoyable basketball game underneath all of this. When we get legitimate games, we have a great time. Those games remind me why I love 2K in the first place.

But then you run into someone turbo-speeding around the court, doing everything at an elite level, and greening absurd fading threes from deep while legitimate players are still trying to consistently hit wide-open shots.

That isn’t competitive basketball.

Until 2K makes a serious effort to deal with cheating on PC and actually demonstrates that cheaters are being detected and removed quickly, I cannot recommend NBA 2K27.

I have not played NBA 2k since 2019.  I will never play this game online or with other people so I don't need to talk about cheaters or racists online.
  
I only bought this game to play with the WNBA players.  
 
The game is not perfect, but for me personally I enjoy the WNBA My player and have enjoyed my game experience so far.  I thank 2k for allowing the WNBA into the game and if they were to ever make a stand-alone WNBA game in the future, I would purchase it.

It is unbelievable how NBA 2K continues to be the exact same game year after year, copy-pasted with the exact same legacy flaws and only a handful of minimal tweaks that sound good in marketing material like "X thousand new animations." What are you people actually working on all year if this is what you release as a full-price, brand-new title?

There are countless issues in this game, but take player tendencies for example. Do you ever actually adjust shooting and touch tendencies and simulate a season to see if the results make any sense? If you did, you would notice that someone like Luka Dončić - who averages 33 points in real life - drops down to 21 points a game in simulation. How is that not an immediate red flag that something is fundamentally broken? This is something I could fix for you for free, yet year after year, it remains completely neglected.

Another issue that completely ruins immersion are generated draft classes. Randomly generated players end up looking like disproportionate, bizarrely scaled monsters. Is it really that hard to scan 50 to 100 real people - even fans who opt in - and build a decent pool of realistic face presets that we can customize with different hair and features? It’s a basic quality-of-life feature that they haven't been able to figure out for over a decade.

When you haven't been capable of fixing simple issues like this for years, focusing only on how to resell the exact same product with a "NEW" sticker attached to squeeze money out of people, it's clear where your priorities are. But the problem is also on us - we keep giving you a chance because of our love for basketball, so we buy the game every year anyway.

We have to draw the line somewhere and say STOP, and today is that day for me. I am requesting a full refund right after posting this, and you will never get another cent from me until you fundamentally change. Thankfully, there are always plenty of good games out there that actually respect their players.
